finding.title: Empty DOC conversion result suppresses antiword fallback
finding.provenance: Actual DocParser.parse with real tracked OLE DOC fixture and generated empty/nonempty DOCX; converter process boundaries substituted. See additional_provenance for separate real LibreOffice integration and antiword stand-in limit.
finding.additional_provenance: Real generated 18,432-byte OLE DOC created by existing runtime soffice from generated DOCX; actual production LibreOffice conversion back to DOCX succeeds, both reader boundaries injected empty, temporary executable stand-in for antiword validates original SHA and emits expected generated text. Real antiword not installed or exercised. Separately, real repository DOC fixture + generated empty DOCX through actual parser chain reproduces empty-first-choice behavior with mocked converter process boundaries.

Durable regression uses real tracked OLE DOC bytes and generated real empty/nonempty DOCX through actual reader cascade; conversion and antiword execution substituted at converter boundaries. 4 tests (2 failing before), validates fallback original input/temporary cleanup, nonempty first choice, empty final result, archive limits and cancellation.
